Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no sending.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 7 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/referral_lifecycle.py
  tests/test_referral_lifecycle.py

SOURCE OF TRUTH: docs/SPEC-autonomous-podcast-loop.md, section "Referrals" and the non-behaviour "must not contact a referred person before their referrer has made an introduction". Read it in the worktree first.

WHY. Past guests refer people. The loop asks for referrals, records them, and follows up. Two constraints from the owner dominate the design:

CONSTRAINT 1 — INTRODUCTION FIRST. A referred person has NOT opted in to hear from Ankit. The system must not contact them until their referrer has made an introduction. Until then the only permitted outreach is to the REFERRER, asking for that introduction. This is the owner's explicit choice over auto-sending using the referrer's name.

CONSTRAINT 2 — ATTRIBUTION MUST BE TRUE. The owner named "referral tracking drifts from reality" as the subtle failure that would rot this system: attribution says a guest came from a referral when they did not, so he thanks the wrong person. Attribution therefore requires evidence and must never be inferred from coincidence (same company, similar timing, a guessed connection).

BUILD server/pipeline/referral_lifecycle.py — stdlib only, pure decision functions. It records and decides; it never sends.

  STATES = ("recorded", "intro_requested", "introduced", "contacted",
            "converted", "declined", "expired")
  INTRO_REMINDER_DAYS = 7      # remind the referrer once, then stop nagging
  REFERRAL_EXPIRY_DAYS = 60    # unconverted and un-introduced referrals expire

  record_referral(*, referrer_id, referred_name, source_evidence, now) -> dict
      source_evidence is REQUIRED and must be non-empty: what proves this
      referral happened (a message id, a transcript timestamp, a form entry).
      A referral without evidence raises ValueError. Attribution without
      evidence is the drift the owner named.

  next_action(referral, *, now) -> dict
      Returns {"action": str, "target": "referrer"|"referred"|None,
      "reason": str}. The rules:
        * state recorded          -> ask the REFERRER for an introduction
        * state intro_requested and INTRO_REMINDER_DAYS elapsed -> ONE reminder
          to the referrer, then no further reminders ever
        * state introduced        -> follow up with the REFERRED person
        * state contacted         -> no automatic action; awaiting their reply
        * converted/declined/expired -> no action
      The action target must NEVER be "referred" while the state is recorded or
      intro_requested. Enforce this in code, not only by convention.

  may_contact_referred(referral) -> (bool, str)
      True only when an introduction has actually been recorded. This is the
      single gate other code must call before any outreach to a referred person.

  attribution_for(guest_id, referrals) -> dict
      Returns {"referred_by": id|None, "evidence": [...], "confident": bool}.
      confident is True only when exactly ONE referral matches with evidence.
      When two referrals claim the same guest, return confident False with both
      listed rather than picking one — a wrong thank-you is the failure mode.

TESTS (tests/test_referral_lifecycle.py; at least 7):
 (1) a newly recorded referral's next action targets the REFERRER, never the referred person;
 (2) NEGATIVE and central: may_contact_referred is False for states recorded and
     intro_requested, and True only after introduced;
 (3) NEGATIVE: record_referral raises when source_evidence is empty or missing;
 (4) exactly one reminder is issued after INTRO_REMINDER_DAYS, and a second
     reminder is never produced no matter how much time passes;
 (5) after introduced, the next action targets the referred person;
 (6) NEGATIVE: two referrals claiming the same guest yield confident False with
     both listed, rather than silently choosing one;
 (7) attribution with a single evidenced referral is confident True;
 (8) NEGATIVE: no state ever produces an action targeting "referred" before
     introduction — assert this by iterating EVERY state, so a future state
     cannot quietly break the rule.
tasks.verified: referred people are never contacted before an introduction, and attribution requires evidence so the wrong person is never thanked

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/promo_schedule.py
  tests/test_promo_schedule.py

SOURCE OF TRUTH: docs/SPEC-autonomous-podcast-loop.md, section "Promotion across the week". Read it in the worktree first.

WHY. An episode publishes Thursday. The owner wants launch-day promotion plus TWO further touches that same week, each using a DIFFERENT clip or angle, and follow-ups must not repeat earlier phrasing for the same episode. Today nothing schedules follow-ups, so promotion is a single launch-day burst.

BUILD server/pipeline/promo_schedule.py — stdlib only, pure functions:

  TOUCHES_PER_WEEK = 3          # launch day plus two follow-ups (owner)
  MIN_HOURS_BETWEEN = 24        # never two touches for one episode in a day

  plan_week(*, publish_at, assets, now=None) -> list[dict]
      `assets` is the pool of available promo material: clips and posts, each
      with an id and an angle/platform. Returns TOUCHES_PER_WEEK scheduled
      touches within the seven days following publish_at, each
      {"when": iso, "asset_id": ..., "angle": ..., "sequence": 1..N}.
      Rules:
        * the first touch is on publish day
        * touches are spread, never closer than MIN_HOURS_BETWEEN
        * every touch uses a DIFFERENT asset. If the pool has fewer assets than
          touches, return only as many touches as there are distinct assets and
          record the shortfall rather than reusing one — silently repeating an
          asset reads as a bot.
        * all touches fall inside the seven days after publish_at
      Deterministic: same inputs give the same plan.

  distinct_enough(candidate_text, previous_texts, *, threshold=0.5) -> (bool, str)
      Rejects a follow-up that repeats earlier phrasing for the same episode.
      Compare with a normalised word-shingle overlap; over `threshold` is a
      repeat. Also reject any shared sentence of 8+ words outright.

  A shortfall (fewer assets than touches) must be visible in the return value,
  never silently absorbed.

TESTS (tests/test_promo_schedule.py; at least 6):
 (1) a full asset pool yields exactly TOUCHES_PER_WEEK touches, first on publish day;
 (2) every touch uses a distinct asset, and all fall within seven days;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a pool with only two assets yields two touches AND a recorded
     shortfall, rather than three with one asset reused;
 (4) no two touches are closer than MIN_HOURS_BETWEEN;
 (5) NEGATIVE: distinct_enough rejects a follow-up sharing a 10-word sentence
     with a previous post;
 (6) distinct_enough accepts genuinely different copy about the same episode;
 (7) determinism: identical inputs produce an identical plan;
 (8) NEGATIVE: an empty asset pool yields zero touches and a shortfall, and does
     not raise.
tasks.verified: three spread touches per week on distinct assets, with a shortfall recorded rather than an asset silently reused
